newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore firms told to raise productivity.
newsitem.headline: Singapore firms told to raise productivity.

text.p: Singapore urged local companies on Saturday to raise productivity and move towards producing higher-value and higher-quality products.

Singapore's Minister of State for Trade, Industry and Communications, Goh Chee Wee, said land and labour would remain scarce resources in Singapore, possibly keeping basic operating costs high relative to other low cost countries.
"This translates into higher-priced products," he said.

"To remain competitive, our companies must raise productivity and move from producing low-value, mediocre-quality products, to higher-value, high-quality products," Goh told businessmen at the opening of a seminar.

He said although it was easy to buy equipment and machinery to make products, "it is how well the equipment is used by workers that determines the output and productivity of the company and the quality of the final products."
Companies that re-train workers to adapt to new technologies and processes would do well in the long run, he said.

He noted that many small and medium-sized companies in Singapore supported larger companies and multinational corporations based here and that the smaller firms tended to have only a few such customers.
"Quite a number of them who continued operating in this mode have been hit by the recent downturn in the electronics industry," he added.
But those firms that had expanded regionally and diversified into other sectors had escaped the brunt of the slowdown, he said.
